body: **Foco:** Contrastes sutis (not so much… as…) — produção e revisão.
**Expressões:** A double-edged sword.
**Pronúncia:** Ritmo e ênfase para nuances.
**24 palavras novas** (discurso público).
**Texto do dia:** e-mail, carta, mensagem.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo produzir e revisar contrastes sutis (not so much… as…, less… than…) num e-mail sobre um discurso, e usar A double-edged sword.

body: Esta aula treina **ouvir e anotar informações (IELTS Listening, TOEFL Listening)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.subject: Re: Draft of the harbor speech
paras: Thank you for the draft. The humor is **a double-edged sword**: the joke about the delayed bridge will **win the hall** but may **cost us the press**. Your instinct is sound; the issue is **not so much the joke as its timing**.

Consider this: the speech should be **less an apology than an account**, and **more a promise than a defense**. **Rather than open with the joke**, begin with the residents. I would also cut the third paragraph, **not because it is weak but because it repeats** the second.
**Could you revert by noon?** The mayor reads it at four. Best, Lucia

items.q: Lucia thinks the joke may be risky.
She wants the speech to open with the joke.
items.why: Rather than open with the joke.

items.q: She would cut the third paragraph because it is weak.
items.why: not because it is weak but because it repeats.
a double-edged sword = algo com vantagens e riscos.
win the hall = conquistar a plateia.

blocks.body: Na **revisão**, procure três erros: **paralelismo** (mesma classe nos dois lados), **repetição** de preposição ou *because*, e **verbo** após *rather than*.
*Not so much because it is weak as it repeats* ✗ → **not so much because it is weak as because it repeats** ✓.

items.s: The issue is not so much the joke ___ its timing. (as)
The speech should be less an apology ___ an account. (than)
___ than open with the joke, begin with the residents. (rather)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.ans: Is the issue the joke itself
items.pt: O problema é a piada em si?

items.ans: Then I will begin with the residents

body: **A double-edged sword** — Faca de dois gumes.
**Win the hall.** — Conquistar a plateia.
**Cost us dearly.** — Sair caro para nós.
**On balance,…** — Em balanço,…
**Rather than…** — Em vez de…
**Sound instinct.** — Instinto acertado.
**Cut to the chase.** — Ir direto ao ponto.
**Read the room.** — Ler o clima do ambiente.
**Strike a balance.** — Encontrar o equilíbrio.
**Better left unsaid.** — Melhor não dizer.
**Is the issue the joke itself?** — O problema é a piada em si?
**Exactly. Humor is a double-edged sword.** — Exato. O humor é uma faca de dois gumes.
**Then I will begin with the residents.** — Então começarei pelos moradores.

forms: Discursos põem a plateia em primeiro plano.

blocks.title: Pronúncia: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances

items.label: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances
items.note: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances: o acento muda o sentido (He said she STOLE it × he said SHE stole it) e as pausas separam ideias técnicas densas.
words: I didn’t SAY he did it.
I didn’t say HE did it.
I didn’t say he DID it.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence email giving feedback on a draft speech, using at least three contrast structures and a double-edged sword.
blocks.model: Dear Karim, thank you for the draft. The problem is not so much the length as the order. It should be less a list than a story. Rather than begin with statistics, begin with one resident’s voice. The anecdote is a double-edged sword: it moves people but can sound staged. Please revert by Thursday.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
